Run exploratory residual PCA summaries

Source: R/api-tables.R, R/api-plotting-dispatch.R
analyze_residual_pca.Rd

Legacy-compatible residual diagnostics can be inspected in two ways:

  1. overall residual PCA on the person x combined-facet matrix

  2. facet-specific residual PCA on person x facet-level matrices

Usage

analyze_residual_pca(
  diagnostics,
  mode = c("overall", "facet", "both"),
  facets = NULL,
  pca_max_factors = 10L,
  parallel = FALSE,
  parallel_reps = 200L,
  parallel_quantile = 0.95,
  parallel_method = c("residual_permutation", "model_bootstrap"),
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_residual_pca'
plot(x, type = "scree", mode = "overall", ...)

Arguments

diagnostics

Output from diagnose_mfrm() or fit_mfrm().

mode

For analyze_residual_pca(): "overall", "facet", or "both".

For plot(): "overall" (default) or "facet". Do not also supply mode when using a prefixed type such as "facet_scree".

facets

Optional subset of facets. This selects the facet-specific analyses and the facets combined to define columns in the overall PCA.

pca_max_factors

Maximum number of components retained for loadings, subject to matrix dimensions; "auto" caps this at 10. Variance tables retain the full eigenvalue spectrum, not only those loading columns.

parallel

Logical; if TRUE, add a simulation reference to the PCA tables.

parallel_reps

Number of permutations or simulated-and-refitted data sets when parallel = TRUE. Each model-bootstrap replicate requires a full fit.

parallel_quantile

Upper reference quantile used as the exploratory comparison cutoff. The default (0.95) follows the common parallel analysis convention.

parallel_method

Reference method. "residual_permutation" (default) permutes standardized residuals within each column, preserving residual distributions and missingness. "model_bootstrap" generates ratings and refits a supported RSM/PCM MML model; supply the original fit, not detached diagnostics. See Model-generated reference below for restrictions.

seed

Optional integer seed for reproducible simulation. When supplied, the caller's random-number state is restored after the calculation.

x

A result from analyze_residual_pca().

type

"scree", "parallel_scree", "parallel_excess", or "loadings". Existing "overall_*" and "facet_*" spellings remain supported.

...

facet selects a facet for mode = "facet" (default: the first available facet); component = 1 selects a loading component; top_n = 20 limits displayed loadings. preset is "standard", "publication", "compact", or "monochrome"; draw = FALSE returns data without drawing.

Value

A named list with:

  • mode: resolved mode used for computation

  • facet_names: facets analyzed

  • overall: overall PCA bundle (or NULL)

  • by_facet: named list of facet PCA bundles

  • overall_table: variance table for overall PCA

  • by_facet_table: stacked variance table across facets

  • parallel_settings, parallel_overall_table, parallel_by_facet_table, and parallel_status: returned for every call; the parallel tables are populated when parallel = TRUE

  • bootstrap_trials, bootstrap_settings: attempted replicate/scope records and generation settings for the model bootstrap; otherwise NULL.

  • errors: explanations for unavailable overall or facet PCA analyses; unavailable analyses have empty variance tables.

  • warnings: named list of non-fatal PCA warnings captured from the underlying PCA engine. These indicate exploratory boundary conditions, not confirmatory evidence.

  • InferenceTier, SupportsFormalInference, PrimaryReportingEligible, ReportingUse, and DecisionUse: machine-readable guards that keep this route exploratory and prohibit an automatic dimensionality or subscore decision.

For plot(): Invisibly, a ggplot object whose plot_data(p) payload contains:

  • plot: "scree", "parallel_scree", "parallel_excess", or "loadings"

  • mode: "overall" or "facet"

  • facet: facet name (or NULL)

  • title: plot title text

  • data: underlying table used for plotting

  • InferenceTier, SupportsFormalInference, PrimaryReportingEligible, ReportingUse, and DecisionUse: machine-readable exploratory-screening guards

Details

Performs exploratory eigenvalue/loading PCA on pairwise-complete standardized residual correlation matrices (overall Person-by-combined-facet and/or facet Person-by-facet-level). Undefined pairwise correlations or non-PSD matrices are recorded in errors without zero-filling or smoothing.

With parallel = TRUE, "residual_permutation" permutes standardized residuals within columns; "model_bootstrap" simulates conditionally independent ratings and refits unanchored unit-weight RSM/PCM MML models with fixed N(0, 1) ability, retaining all attempted replicates in bootstrap_trials and withholding cutoffs (ParallelMean, ParallelCutoff, ExcessOverParallelCutoff, ExceedsParallelCutoff) if any replicate fails. Reference quantiles are exploratory componentwise screens rather than multiplicity-calibrated dimensionality tests; pass residual_pca = "none" to diagnose_mfrm() when calling analyze_residual_pca() separately.

plot() method: Plot saved residual PCA

Display a saved residual PCA or its saved parallel-analysis comparison. Plotting does not generate a new parallel reference.

Fitting before a separate PCA

Use diagnose_mfrm(fit, residual_pca = "none") when PCA will be requested separately with analyze_residual_pca(..., mode = "both"), avoiding duplicate PCA calculation. Inspect the tables/plots above with the model's fit diagnostics.

Reading PCA plots

Start with overall mode, then facet views. "scree" shows eigenvalues; "parallel_scree" adds saved means/cutoffs, and "parallel_excess" plots observed-minus-cutoff. First compute references with parallel = TRUE; inspect parallel_status/bootstrap_trials and distinguish permutation from refitted bootstrap. "loadings" selects largest absolute loadings; read both signs and magnitudes. These reuse the exploratory evidence described above; multiple views neither provide independent evidence nor prove dimensionality.

References

The residual-PCA idea follows the Rasch residual-structure literature, especially Linacre's discussions of principal components of Rasch residuals. The current mfrmr implementation should be interpreted as an exploratory extension for many-facet workflows rather than as a direct reproduction of a single FACETS/Winsteps output table.

The optional parallel analysis follows Horn's data-driven eigenvalue comparison logic and later recommendations to compare observed eigenvalues with high quantiles of a reference distribution. Here that reference is generated by within-column permutation of standardized residuals by default. The optional model bootstrap instead regenerates ratings and refits the supported model. The cited factor-retention literature does not calibrate either many-facet residual comparison as a fitted-model test.

  • Horn, J. L. (1965). A rationale and test for the number of factors in factor analysis. Psychometrika, 30, 179-185. doi:10.1007/BF02289447 .

  • Glorfeld, L. W. (1995). An improvement on Horn's parallel analysis methodology for selecting the correct number of factors to retain. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 55, 377-393. doi:10.1177/0013164495055003002 .

  • Hayton, J. C., Allen, D. G., & Scarpello, V. (2004). Factor retention decisions in exploratory factor analysis: A tutorial on parallel analysis. Organizational Research Methods, 7, 191-205.

  • Timmerman, M. E., & Lorenzo-Seva, U. (2011). Dimensionality assessment of ordered polytomous items with parallel analysis. Psychological Methods, 16, 209-220.

  • Linacre, J. M. (1998). Structure in Rasch residuals: Why principal components analysis (PCA)? Rasch Measurement Transactions, 12(2), 636. https://www.rasch.org/rmt/rmt122m.htm

  • Linacre, J. M. (1998). Detecting multidimensionality: Which residual data-type works best? Journal of Outcome Measurement, 2(3), 266-283.

See also

diagnose_mfrm(), plot(x, type = "residual_pca"), mfrmr_visual_diagnostics

analyze_residual_pca(), mfrmr_plot_migration

Examples

# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_core.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
diag <- diagnose_mfrm(fit, residual_pca = "none")
pca <- analyze_residual_pca(diag, mode = "both")
# A fitted model is also accepted: analyze_residual_pca(fit, mode = "both").
summary(pca)
#> Residual PCA summary
#> 
#> Overview
#>  Analysis Facets Overall components Facet component rows
#>      both      2                 16                    8
#> 
#> Residual eigenvalues
#>  PC Eigenvalue Proportion
#>   1      2.114      0.132
#>   2      1.833      0.115
#>   3      1.706      0.107
#>   4      1.519      0.095
#>   5      1.290      0.081
#>   6      1.157      0.072
#>   7      1.098      0.069
#>   8      1.054      0.066
#>   9      0.949      0.059
#>  10      0.846      0.053
#> Residual PCA is exploratory residual-structure screening (overall and/or by facet), not a standalone dimensionality test or an automatic decision about dimensions or subscores. 
p <- plot(pca, type = "scree", mode = "overall", draw = FALSE)
head(plot_data(p, "data"))
#>   Component Eigenvalue Proportion Cumulative
#> 1         1   2.113557 0.13209732  0.1320973
#> 2         2   1.832887 0.11455546  0.2466528
#> 3         3   1.706239 0.10663995  0.3532927
#> 4         4   1.519039 0.09493995  0.4482327
#> 5         5   1.289992 0.08062450  0.5288572
#> 6         6   1.157287 0.07233045  0.6011876
# Optional permutation reference repeats the PCA calculation.
# example("analyze_residual_pca", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pca_pa <- analyze_residual_pca(diag, mode = "overall", parallel = TRUE, parallel_reps = 10)
head(pca_pa$overall_table)
} # }
head(pca$overall_table)
#>   Component Eigenvalue Proportion Cumulative
#> 1         1   2.113557 0.13209732  0.1320973
#> 2         2   1.832887 0.11455546  0.2466528
#> 3         3   1.706239 0.10663995  0.3532927
#> 4         4   1.519039 0.09493995  0.4482327
#> 5         5   1.289992 0.08062450  0.5288572
#> 6         6   1.157287 0.07233045  0.6011876
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("plot.mfrm_residual_pca", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ratings_all <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
selected_people <- unique(ratings_all$Person)[1:24]
ratings <- ratings_all[
  ratings_all$Person %in% selected_people, , drop = FALSE]
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                method = "JML")
diag <- diagnose_mfrm(fit, residual_pca = "overall")
pca <- analyze_residual_pca(diag, mode = "overall")
plt <- plot(pca, type = "scree", draw = FALSE)
head(plot_data(plt, "data"))
# Ten replicates illustrate the display, not a stable reference cutoff.
pca_pa <- analyze_residual_pca(diag, mode = "overall", parallel = TRUE,
                               parallel_reps = 10, seed = 2026)
pa <- plot(pca_pa, type = "parallel_scree", draw = FALSE)
head(plot_data(pa, "data"))
plt_load <- plot(pca, type = "loadings", component = 1, draw = FALSE)
head(plot_data(plt_load, "data"))
if (interactive()) {
  plot(pca, type = "scree", preset = "publication")
}
} # }
